content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To prevent an ascaris infection, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase a heavy-duty vegetable scrubbing brush (15 minutes)
Step 2. Sanitize the food preparation surfaces with bleach solution (20 minutes)
Step 3. Rinse the peeled root vegetables under high-pressure filtered water (5 minutes)
Step 4. Soak the scrubbed vegetables in a vinegar-water solution (15 minutes)
Step 5. Boil the drinking water for at least one minute to ensure safety (10 minutes)
Step 6. Wash your hands thoroughly with antimicrobial soap and warm water (2 minutes)
Step 7. Dispose of any potentially contaminated soil or fertilizer (30 minutes)
Step 8. Inspect the produce for any visible dirt or damage (10 minutes)
Step 9. Research local soil quality and known parasite prevalence (2 hours)
Step 10. Consult with a community health officer about local risks (45 minutes)
Step 11. Distribute educational pamphlets on hygiene to the household (30 minutes)
Step 12. Install a high-micron water filtration system on the main tap (4 hours)
Step 13. Seal all prepared food in airtight, parasite-proof containers (10 minutes)
Step 14. Gather all necessary cleaning supplies and protective gloves (20 minutes)
Step 15. Cook all vegetables to an internal temperature of 140°F (30 minutes)
Step 16. Label the filtered water containers clearly (5 minutes)
Step 17. Clean the kitchen sink with a concentrated disinfectant (15 minutes)
Step 18. Scrub the fingernails using a dedicated nail brush (5 minutes)
Step 19. Wash all utensils used during raw food preparation in a dishwasher (1 hour)
Step 20. Fence off the kitchen garden to prevent animal access (6 hours)
Step 21. Remove jewelry and watches before starting food prep (2 minutes)
Step 22. Dry the cleaned vegetables with a single-use paper towel (5 minutes)
Step 23. Sweep and mop the kitchen floor to remove tracked-in eggs (40 minutes)
Step 24. Launder all cleaning cloths in hot water and high heat (1.5 hours)
Step 25. Peel the skin off all raw root vegetables (10 minutes)
Step 26. Clean the cutting boards using a stiff brush and hot soapy water (10 minutes)
Step 27. Disinfect the doorknobs and cabinet handles (20 minutes)
Step 28. Purchase a set of color-coded cutting boards (30 minutes)
Step 29. Review the latest sanitation guidelines from the WHO (1 hour)
Step 30. Sterilize the vegetable scrubbing brush in boiling water (10 minutes)
Step 31. Attend a seminar on tropical disease prevention (4 hours)
Step 32. Buy bottled water for emergency backup use (45 minutes)
Step 33. Organize the pantry to separate raw and cooked goods (1 hour)
Step 34. Harvest the vegetables from the garden (30 minutes)
Step 35. Sort the produce by type and required cleaning intensity (20 minutes)
Step 36. Clear the countertop of all non-essential items (15 minutes)
Step 37. Document the cleaning schedule on a kitchen calendar (10 minutes)
Step 38. Interview a local veterinarian about pet parasite control (30 minutes)
Step 39. Purchase a supply of liquid hand soap and paper towels (30 minutes)
Step 40. Wash all fruit that will be eaten raw (15 minutes)
Step 41. Inventory the current household medical kit (20 minutes)
Step 42. Put on clean clothes and a protective apron (10 minutes)
Step 43. Purchase a thermometer for monitoring cooking temperatures (15 minutes)
Step 44. Inspect the water filtration system for leaks (15 minutes)
Step 45. Bathe and scrub thoroughly after handling soil (20 minutes)
Step 46. Final check of the kitchen hygiene protocol (5 minutes)
Step 47. Schedule a follow-up hygiene inspection (15 minutes)
Step 48. Download a food safety monitoring mobile app (5 minutes)
Step 49. Put on a pair of waterproof work gloves (2 minutes)
Step 50. Post hand-washing signs above every sink (15 minutes)
Step 51. Survey the property for proper drainage and waste disposal (3 hours)
Step 52. Remove any standing water where waste could accumulate (1 hour)
Step 53. Conduct a thorough deep-clean of the entire house (8 hours)
Step 54. Wipe down all appliances with disinfectant (30 minutes)
Step 55. Train household members on proper waste disposal (1 hour)
Step 56. Mop the bathroom floor with a bleach-based cleaner (30 minutes)
Step 57. Set up a dedicated hand-washing station near the entrance (45 minutes)
Step 58. Record the completion of the prevention protocol (5 minutes)
Step 59. Install a shoe rack outside the door to prevent tracking dirt (30 minutes)
Step 60. Mix a fresh batch of sanitizing solution (5 minutes)
Step 61. Store the sorting bins in a clean cupboard (5 minutes)
Step 62. Calibrate the food thermometer (10 minutes)
Step 63. Order a soil testing kit online (15 minutes)
Step 64. Vacuum all carpets and area rugs (1 hour)
Step 65. Replace the air filters in the ventilation system (20 minutes)
Step 66. Read the instruction manual for the new cleaning equipment (30 minutes)
Step 67. Wash the garden tools with a hose and detergent (20 minutes)
Step 68. Dispose of the trash in a sealed outdoor bin (10 minutes)
Step 69. Buy a new set of outdoor gardening shoes (30 minutes)
Step 70. Take a shower to remove any environmental dust (15 minutes)
